papers.title_en: SAP-Depth: Scene-Adaptive Probability Framework for Self-Supervised Monocular Depth Estimation
papers.authors: Bowen He, Li Zhang, Yujie Chen, Chang Cheng
papers.evidence: 自监督单目深度估计与自适应深度分布
papers.tldr: 自监督单目深度估计仍受细粒度细节丢失和场景结构适应不足困扰。SAP-Depth 提出场景自适应概率框架，利用可学习参数预测器驱动动态分箱机制，根据输入图像上下文自适应估计场景特定深度分布。其分箱概率解码器融合多尺度表示，预测稠密深度概率，从而增强边界锐度和结构恢复能力。在 KITTI 上该方法精度优于现有先进方法，尤其能更好保留复杂边缘细节，并在 Make3D 上验证了泛化性与鲁棒性。
papers.abstract_en: Self-supervised monocular depth estimation remains challenging due to the loss of fine-grained details and limited adaptability to varying scene structures. In this paper, we propose SAP-Depth, a novel architecture based on Scene-Adaptive Probabilistic. Unlike traditional methods, we introduce a Dynamic Bins mechanism powered by a Learnable Parameter Predictor, which adaptively estimates scene-specific depth distributions conditioned on the input image context. Furthermore, a Bin-wise Probability Distribution Decoder is designed to effectively fuse multi-scale representations to predict dense depth probability distributions, significantly enhancing boundary sharpness and structural recovery. Through the collaborative coupling of these proposed modules, our model achieves dynamic prediction of scene-specific depth distributions. Extensive experiments on the KITTI dataset show that SAP-Depth outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in accuracy, particularly in its ability to better preserve complex edge details. Further, tests on the Make3D dataset validate the model's excellent generalization capability and robustness.

papers.title_en: VideoMaMa++: Temporally Consistent Video Matting via Preserve-and-Refine Token
papers.authors: Sangbeom Lim, Seoung Wug Oh, Heeji Yoon, Seungryong Kim, Joon-Young Lee
papers.evidence: 无需 trimap 的时序一致视频抠图
papers.tldr: 扩散式视频抠图受算力限制，通常只能处理6至24帧短片段，长视频分块独立抠图会造成边界闪烁和透明度不连续。VideoMaMa++将RGB与掩码表示为独立token流，通过全时空自注意力自适应融合纹理与布局，并引入可学习的preserve/refine token实现滑动窗口推理。它把已生成matte跨块传播，并用全局参考锚点抑制长序列误差累积。在标准基准和真实长视频上，该方法在细节精度与时序一致性上优于现有扩散式方法，且无需额外训练即可保持跨块一致。
papers.abstract_en: Diffusion-based video matting has recently emerged as a leading approach, leveraging video diffusion priors from internet-scale pretraining to achieve strong zero-shot generalization from limited synthetic data. However, the heavy compute of these diffusion backbones limits inference to a short chunk of just 6 to 24 frames, so even ordinary videos span multiple chunks. Because each chunk is matted independently from coarse mask guidance, existing methods fail to maintain consistency across chunk boundaries, producing flickering edges and discontinuous transparency. We address this with a mask-guided diffusion-matting framework built on two ideas. The RGB and mask conditioning are represented as separate token streams that interact through full spatio-temporal self-attention, letting the model adaptively combine fine RGB texture with coarse mask layout rather than committing to a fixed channel-wise fusion. On top of this, we propose a novel pair of learnable embeddings, the preserve token and the refine token, that act as a per-frame conditioning interface and enable a sliding-window inference scheme in which already-generated mattes are propagated across chunk boundaries for local temporal consistency, complemented by a globally shared reference anchor at every chunk to prevent error accumulation in long sequences without any additional training. Across standard video matting benchmarks and in-the-wild long footage, our framework outperforms prior diffusion-based methods in both fine-detail accuracy and temporal consistency, and uniquely maintains consistency across chunk boundaries on long videos.

papers.title_en: CorrCLIPv2: Harnessing Unlabeled Images for Open-Vocabulary Semantic Segmentation
papers.authors: Dengke Zhang, Fagui Liu, Quan Tang, C. L. Philip Chen
papers.evidence: 免训练开放词汇语义分割框架
papers.tldr: 开放词汇语义分割需摆脱固定类别限制，但CLIP的像素级识别受类间patch交互噪声干扰。CorrCLIPv2提出免训练、以对象为中心的统一框架，从patch相关性、特征表示和输出正则三方面改进，并引入跨图像对象检索与多CLIP集成。实验在10个基准上达到新SOTA，并在22个多域数据集上超过全监督开放词汇方法，显示利用无标注图像提升分割鲁棒性的价值。
papers.abstract_en: Open-vocabulary semantic segmentation aims to classify pixels without being restricted to a fixed set of categories. Although Contrastive Language-Image Pre-training (CLIP) demonstrates remarkable potential for open-vocabulary recognition, its segmentation capability is impaired by noisy inter-class patch interactions. To this end, this work proposes a unified training-free object-centric framework, named CorrCLIPv2, from three complementary aspects of patch correlation, feature representation, and output regularization. Specifically, for patch correlation, we leverage class-agnostic mask generators to explicitly disentangle inter-class interactions. Moreover, we utilize spatially-coherent features from self-supervised models to compute attention scores to mitigate mask inaccuracies. Regarding feature representation, we devise a refinement mechanism to simultaneously strengthen spatial details and semantic representation. Within the output space, we unify predictions via voting in each mask to enhance spatial consistency. To mitigate contextual bias and enhance prediction accuracy of objects, we further extend the framework by incorporating a cross-image object retrieval paradigm, which incurs minimal computational overhead. We build a memory bank of CorrCLIP-enhanced features from unlabeled images and implement a regime of multi-CLIP ensemble. By aggregating semantically consistent object features across diverse contexts retrieved from the memory bank, CorrCLIPv2 mitigates context-induced interference and obtains more robust predictions. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our approach establishes a new state-of-the-art on 10 standard benchmarks. Remarkably, it even surpasses fully supervised open-vocabulary methods across 22 multi-domain datasets. Code is available at: https://github.com/zdk258/CorrCLIP.

papers.title_en: Editing Images into Reusable Layers via Compositional Edit-Prior Distillation
papers.authors: Wen Xue, Yong Liu, Xueheng Li, Si Wu, Yong Xu, Yipeng Sun, Yan Li, Simiu Gu
papers.evidence: 生成可复用RGBA图层，含alpha通道的图层分解
papers.tldr: 现有图像编辑模型输出扁平结果，难以精确局部操控和复用图层，而分解方法又与指令编辑分离。为此提出LayerEditor，用In-Context RGB-Alpha Token Modeling在单一token序列中联合建模编辑画布与有序RGBA图层，并通过Compositional Edit-Prior Distillation保留预训练编辑先验。作者构建LayerEditor-100K数据集与分层编辑基准。实验表明该方法在保持编辑保真度的同时生成准确RGBA图层，支持图层级操控与多图层分解。
papers.abstract_en: High-quality image editing requires precise modification of target regions while preserving the content of unrelated regions. Existing editing models produce flattened outputs that limit precise local manipulation and layer reuse, while decomposition methods typically optimize layer recovery separately from instruction-driven editing. To this end, we introduce LayerEditor, a unified framework that couples instruction-guided image editing with controllable generation of reusable RGBA layers. At its core, In-Context RGB-Alpha Token Modeling jointly represents the edited canvas and an ordered sequence of RGB-Alpha layers within a single token sequence, enabling semantic edits and explicit control over individual layer content. To retain the pretrained model's editing capability during adaptation to layered outputs, we propose Compositional Edit-Prior Distillation, which transfers its editing prior to both the edited canvas and the image composed from the predicted layers. To support training and evaluation, we construct LayerEditor-100K, a large-scale paired image-editing dataset with ordered RGBA layer annotations, and introduce dedicated benchmarks for layered editing. Extensive experiments demonstrate that LayerEditor maintains strong editing fidelity while generating accurate RGBA layers, supporting both flexible layer-level manipulation and multi-layer decomposition.
